ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Joe Louis Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for persecutory thoughts and poor sleep two weeks after a collapse in the street: a nonjudgmental assessment of cocaine use, the differential of psychosis, a cognitive screen, safety, cardiovascular risk, harm reduction and money worries. Concerns: He feels he is being followed and cannot sleep, and wants to feel like himself again; He is worried about his heart and his mind after collapsing in the street; He worries about money and does not want his family burdened. [S]

Financial insecurity: years of tax debt from his time as a well-paid athlete, now settled, left him with no savings; irregular income from paid appearances; worry about money keeps him awake: active, confirmed [S]
Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) for three days; rapid tests negative for influenza and COVID-19; resolved within ten days without antibiotics: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care for persecutory thoughts and poor sleep two weeks after a collapse in the street: a nonjudgmental assessment of cocaine use, the differential of psychosis, a cognitive screen, safety, cardiovascular risk, harm reduction and money worries
One-week review, seen the same day by addiction psychiatry: the diagnosis, an antipsychotic, contingency management and cognitive behavioral therapy
Four-week review: psychotic symptoms, urine tests, blood pressure and a diagnosis of hypertension
Ten-week review: remission, the antipsychotic taper, cognition off cocaine, the echocardiogram and a one-day return to use
Fifteen-week review off the antipsychotic: recovery, blood pressure and finances
Same-day sick visit for a cold

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: A nonjudgmental assessment: DSM-5-TR criteria, the DAST-10 and AUDIT-C, and a urine drug test (with fentanyl) done only with his consent and explained as part of care; person-first language; his own goals first
Addiction psychiatry consultation to settle the diagnosis, advise on an antipsychotic and plan treatment for cocaine use disorder

Differential diagnosis of the psychotic symptoms: follow their course after the last cocaine use; MoCA now and again when he is well; TSH, vitamin B12, HIV and syphilis tests; brain MRI because the symptoms are new after age 50 in a man with years of head impacts; traumatic encephalopathy syndrome is a research diagnosis with no clinical test, and no such label is given; a structured assessment that guards against the documented bias toward diagnosing schizophrenia in Black men
Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline saved in his phone, written criteria for urgent care, and safety review at every visit
Harm reduction: fentanyl can be in cocaine; naloxone nasal spray and fentanyl test strips, never using alone, and the clinic's open door after any use

Aripiprazole 5 mg daily for persecutory beliefs that persist after ten days without cocaine; weight, blood pressure, glucose and lipids, akathisia and movement checks under the APA guideline; a gradual taper after a period of remission

Contingency management with twice-weekly urine tests for twelve weeks and prize draws for negative results, with weekly cognitive behavioral therapy; no medicine is approved by the FDA for cocaine use disorder, and off-label medicines are held back while he does well, since the stimulant-based ones are unsafe after psychosis and with high blood pressure

Cardiovascular risk from cocaine: ECG and creatine kinase today; blood pressure at every visit and a home monitor with twice-daily readings for a week before the four-week visit; call 911 for chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness or tearing pain in the chest or back; beta-blockers avoided while he may still use cocaine

Hypertension: amlodipine 5 mg daily with a target below 130/80 mmHg; urine albumin; an echocardiogram for left ventricular hypertrophy that also measures the aortic root and ascending aorta; abdominal aortic ultrasound not indicated before 65 in a man who has never smoked

Money worries: the clinic social worker helps with a budget, benefits he may qualify for as a veteran, and a free review of his tax records by a Low Income Taxpayer Clinic, with the Taxpayer Advocate Service if any federal tax problem is found
Family involvement only with his consent: he chooses whom, if anyone, to involve and what may be shared; the clinic contacts no one without his permission unless his life is in danger
Sleep: regular hours, no cocaine and little alcohol, light in the morning and a dark room at night; no sleeping pill while he may use cocaine or alcohol
Persecutory fears gone and six or more hours of sleep
No persecutory beliefs by four weeks; sleeping six to seven hours
No cocaine use, his goal, with contingency management and cognitive behavioral therapy
No use for six weeks, one day of use at week seven reported by him, none since; 22 of 24 scheduled urine tests done, 21 negative
154/98 at intake, 146/92 at diagnosis, 126/78 on amlodipine
A clear answer about his memory and thinking once he is well
MoCA 25 during symptoms, 27 after ten weeks; brain MRI normal; no neurocognitive disorder
A plan for money that lets him sleep
Budget made with the social worker; a free tax clinic review confirmed no money owed; benefits checked

list.item: Independent in all activities; has cancelled several appearances in the past month because of fear and fatigue [S]

Alert and oriented; courteous and watchful, sitting where he can see the door; speech normal in rate; mood worried and tired; a fixed belief that people are following him and plan to harm him, with partial insight (he wonders aloud whether the cocaine is part of it); no hallucinations; no thoughts of harming himself or anyone else; no confusion; MoCA 25 with points lost on attention and delayed recall after three hours of sleep [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-07-13: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with weekly visits and a phone check in three days. He has persecutory beliefs but no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone, no command hallucinations, no plan to act against the people he fears, and he is caring for himself, so he does not need hospital care now; criteria for urgent care were written down with him (thoughts of harming himself or anyone else, acting on the fears, hallucinations, confusion, chest pain or not sleeping at all for two nights). Risk factors reviewed: cocaine use, persecutory beliefs, poor sleep, money worries and a recent collapse. No firearms in the home. A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
